key_insight: Free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals generate linearly polarized X-rays with polarization controlled by crystal orientation, enabling a proposed table-top alternative to synchrotron-based spectroscopy.
engineering_relevance: Compact polarized X-ray sources could make material characterization for photovoltaics, catalysis and optoelectronics more accessible; this is not an AI or solar-cell device study.
method: Theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate polarized X-ray generation from electron-driven van der Waals crystals.
Reorient the crystal to tune polarization without additional polarizers.
Propose orientation-controlled XANES (ORIXANES) using broader-linewidth polarized X-rays.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high polarization across perpendicular-to-in-plane angles and intensities exceeding 10^9 photons s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ mA⁻¹, while presenting synchrotron-comparable table-top XANES as a proposed scheme.
watch_item: Practical ORIXANES performance and the effect of broader spectral linewidths require validation beyond the source demonstration described in the abstract.
paper_title: Polarized X-rays from table-top free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals
